newsitem.title: USA: LINCOLN NATIONAL NEAR AMER. STATES DEAL - SOURCES.
newsitem.headline: LINCOLN NATIONAL NEAR AMER. STATES DEAL - SOURCES.

text.p: Lincoln National Corp is close to finding a buyer for its American States Financial Corp unit and may announce a deal for more than $2 billion as early as next week, sources familiar with the situation said.

Top contenders for the commercial property-casualty business were believed to include Hartford Financial Services Group Inc, Travelers Property Casualty Corp, Germany's Allianz AG Holding, SAFECO Corp and the U.K.'s General Accident Plc, sources said.
However, some sources said they believed Travelers has dropped out of the bidding.
Lincoln National, which has an 83 percent stake in American States, declined comment.
Hartford, Travelers and General Accident declined comment. SAFECO was not immediately available, but has previously declined comment.
Allianz was not immediately available for comment.
Zurich Insurance Co also has been reported to be interested in American States.
But reports that Zurich is in talks to buy mutual fund firm Scudder Stevens & Clark may make Zurich a less likely buyer of American States, an analyst said.
Sources said CNA Financial Corp also had expressed interest, but believe the company has since dropped out of the running. CNA declined comment.
"I think that what we've heard is that a decision will be made next week," one source familiar with the situation said.

The deal has attracted more interest than first expected as insurers, struggling for growth and faced with few attractive acquisition targets, remain unshaken by the property's rich valuation, analysts said.
"There are a couple of companies out there that need acquisitions for critical mass or to make them more important players geographically," Dillon Read analyst Michael Lewis said.
"It is a little expensive," Lewis said. "But there are no bargains in this sector right now."
